answer.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure creates urgency, but memory_73 and exp_73 clearly demonstrate that targeted promotional pricing on SMB segments drives acquisition while destroying cohort durability—explicitly warning against generalizing discounting as sustainable strategy. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well but only in established customers, offering no defense against price-sensitive churn. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is correct for enterprise only, not SMB. Simplifying onboarding (memory_86, memory_31) has proven durable for SMB activation but does not directly address retention of price-sensitive accounts already at risk. Activation messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and nudged first meaningful action—the core mechanism to increase product value perception and stickiness independent of price. This addresses the root problem: price-sensitive churn occurs when customers have not yet experienced sufficient value. By intensifying activation messaging, we increase the probability that at-risk accounts discover deep value before renewal, making price a weaker defection driver. This is a standard-experiment scale (pilot messaging refresh and cadence with cohorts at churn risk) that preserves uncertainty about generalization while testing whether higher engagement can offset price pressure on retention—the metric that matters most for sustainable qualified revenue.
